svg.text: How big an LLM fits a DGX Spark cluster (and what decode speed to expect)
FP4/NVFP4 checkpoints ~ 0.5 GB per B params. A single Spark shows roughly 120 GB to the GPU, about 104 GB after OS overhead.
ONE SPARK - 128 GB unified, ~120 GB GPU-visible, 273 GB/s
gpt-oss-120b MXFP4 (59 GiB): 55-60 tok/s decode, 1,725-1,956 tok/s prefill. NVIDIA rates the box for models up to 200B FP4.
Qwen3.5-35B-A3B NVFP4 (19.8 GiB): 51-72 tok/s. Qwen3.8-27B: 34 tok/s. DeepSeek V4 Flash IQ2: 28-31 tok/s at 131K context.
Dense warning: Llama 3.1 70B FP8 = 2.7 tok/s (LMSYS). A 70B Q4 (~40 GB) fits, but 273 GB/s splits across weights plus KV.
Also fits: Llama 3.3 70B Q8, Gemma 4 12B at 31.8 tok/s, any 8B-14B class with huge context headroom.
TWO SPARKS - ~240 GB pool over ConnectX-7 200 GbE RDMA
Qwen3-235B-A22B FP4: 11.7 tok/s (NVIDIA official). 405B FP4 class reachable per NVIDIA and ASUS two-box positioning.
DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark: ~60-67 tok/s single-stream with up to 1M context. GLM-5.3 Flash: ~22 tok/s (community).
Prefill on 235B FP4 hits 23,477 tok/s in TensorRT-LLM - the Spark's Blackwell compute is far stronger than its decode bus.
FOUR SPARKS - ~480 GB pool, NVIDIA-validated to 700B parameters
700B-class MoE models fit at FP4. Llama 3.3 70B TP=4 shows ~4x the per-token speed of one box for stretched models.
Batched serving scales near-linearly: ~18,400 tok/s on one node to ~74,600 tok/s on four (NVIDIA, Mar 2026).
SIX TO EIGHT SPARKS - community racks past 750B
GLM-5.2 753B: 7.4 tok/s on 6 nodes. Mimo 2.6 Pro 1020B-A42B: 68.3 tok/s on 8 Sparks with DFlash speculative decoding.
Rule of thumb from operators: cluster for capacity and concurrency, not single-stream speed on models that already fit.
Sources: NVIDIA product page and Technical Blog, StorageReview, llamaperf.com, Level1Techs, NVIDIA Developer Forums (2x DSpark, 6-node build) - all links in the post.
